summary.intent: Land a batch of docs and refactor PRs for the monokl repo (decision log, ADR 0005, docs matching the binary, one language definition), then upgrade the pinned Callisto release tooling from 0.17.0 to 0.20.0.
summary.outcome: Four PRs (#91-#94) were opened and ready, with CI partly pending. The Callisto 0.17.0 to 0.20.0 upgrade was handed to an agent along with an intent trail (371), but it had not finished or been verified by the end of the transcript.

repo: Language facts (extensions, test-file rules, Language::of, rules(), is_test_file, is_test_path) now live once in analysis/lang.rs and are read by text search, the pipeline filter, both analyzers and rank.
A hidden `monokl language-rules` subcommand lets rg-compare.py and bench.py read language rules from the binary, avoiding a generated JSON file that could go stale.
`--language python` now exits 2 with the valid values; before it exited 0 with a diagnostic.

Docs had drifted from the binary: README finalScore examples were stale, and ARCHITECTURE/PRINCIPLES described unbuilt features (cache, DashMap, 3-phase index, symbols/refs, blake3) as current. These were moved to "Planned" lists.
Docs gates include `just typos`, `just check-drift`, `just changesets`, `just zizmor`, `just verify-release`, and `just ci`. The rg-compare gate in CONTRIBUTING is 0.9, not 0.

Callisto 0.20 requires the Callisto binary and the release action to be the same version. Pins live in `.prototools`, the generated release workflow, and the setup-callisto/callisto-action/callisto-validate commits in ci.yml.
The generated release workflow has two deliberate deviations to preserve: the `ref: ${{ github.sha }}` checkout (for E170) and a zizmor ignore comment.
Main's tests don't compile without PR #90's fix branch, so docs/refactor branches that build code had to merge it first.
ADR 0005 counts: 87 non-test lines in 11 files read lines or text; 7 fix/test commits across 3 PRs (#66, #68, #77), not the "about 8" in the original brief.
workflow: Parallel agents producing overlapping docs PRs (#93 and #94 both edit README.md, core-types.md, language-analyzer-contract.md) will create merge conflicts; plan merge order up front.
Agents should drop figures they cannot re-derive (e.g. the "about 3.0M fuzzer inputs") rather than carry unverified numbers into the decision log.
Validate a refactor by comparing old and new release binaries across many queries (236 here, identical on 235 with one intended difference).
Intent trails group related release work (trail 371 holds #49, #53 and the Callisto upgrade); agents link to an existing trail instead of creating a new one.

friction: PR #93 asserts `--language python` prints a "not supported" help line, which #94 makes false, so the two PRs contradict each other.
PR #90 has not been merged and blocks main's tests from compiling, forcing agents to merge its branch into their own.
CI on all four PRs was still pending when checked, so none could be called green.
scripts/bench.py was only py_compile-checked and not run end to end in #94.
The ADR's brief had an inaccurate commit count (about 8 vs 7).
open_items: Resolve the #93/#94 docs conflicts, and fix the `--language python` wording once #94 merges.
Decide whether to keep the hidden `monokl language-rules` subcommand or switch to a generated JSON file.
Verify the Callisto 0.20.0 upgrade diff and the rendered changelog once the agent finishes; run `just ci`, `just verify-release 0.4.0` and the other checks.
Check release PR #59 regenerates in the new grouped Major/Minor/Patch layout, and read its changelog before suggesting a merge.
Next code work: "structure from the AST" PR (a `name` field on blocks and a typed `ParsedTerm`), after #93 and #94 land.
After ADR 0005 is accepted, do the span-based identity refactor in up to three PRs, guarded by the harness.
Not measured for ADR 0005: memory and time cost of spans and the second find_iter pass, the harness effect of byte-based dedup, and lossy-decode offset mapping.
Add one-sentence Breaking:/Action: notes to unreleased changesets that remove or change API or flags.
